description: Subject and verb do not agree in number
exampleBad: The number of people are increasing.
exampleGood: The number of people is increasing.
fix: Use singular verb 'is' with 'the number of'; use plural verb with 'a number of'.

description: Incorrect or missing article (a, an, the)
exampleBad: Government should take action to protect environment.
exampleGood: The government should take action to protect the environment.
fix: Use 'the' for specific or previously mentioned nouns; use 'a/an' for first introduction of countable singular nouns.
Memorise common prepositional phrases: depend on, consist of, result in, contribute to.

description: Unnecessary shift in verb tense within a paragraph
exampleBad: Technology advanced rapidly and changes our daily lives.
exampleGood: Technology has advanced rapidly and has changed our daily lives.
fix: Maintain consistent tense throughout a paragraph unless describing different time periods.

description: Words combined in an unnatural way
exampleBad: This problem makes a strong damage to society.
exampleGood: This problem causes significant damage to society.
fix: Learn common IELTS collocations: cause/inflict damage, make/have an impact, play a role.

description: Word used in wrong context or with wrong meaning
exampleBad: People are very economic about saving money.
exampleGood: People are very economical about saving money.
fix: Distinguish between similar words: economic (relating to economics) vs economical (saving money).

description: Body paragraph lacks a clear topic sentence
exampleBad: There are many reasons. People work hard. They also want more money. The companies benefit too.
exampleGood: One major reason is economic motivation. Employees work harder when they believe their efforts will be financially rewarded, and companies benefit from increased productivity.
fix: Start each body paragraph with a clear topic sentence that directly addresses the question.

exampleBad: Furthermore, this is good. Furthermore, people like it. Furthermore, it helps society.
exampleGood: Moreover, this approach benefits individuals. In addition, society as a whole stands to gain. Beyond this, the long-term effects could be transformative.
fix: Vary connective language: Additionally / Moreover / Furthermore / Beyond this / What is more.

description: Essay does not clearly state the writer's position
exampleBad: There are advantages and disadvantages. Some people agree and some disagree. It is a complex issue.
exampleGood: While there are merits to both sides, I firmly believe that the benefits of this policy outweigh its drawbacks.
fix: State your position clearly in the introduction and reaffirm it in the conclusion.

description: Example given is not relevant to the point being made
exampleBad: Technology makes people less social. For example, the iPhone was invented in 2007.
exampleGood: Technology can isolate people from face-to-face interaction. For instance, many young people now prefer to communicate via messaging apps rather than meeting in person.
fix: Ensure each example directly supports your topic sentence and is relevant to the argument.
